title: MedOptm: Compact Vision-Language Reasoning for Clinical VQA
subtitle: Sub-2B parameter clinical visual question answering via convolutional token compression and small language models.
problem: Standard multimodal foundation models (7B-70B parameters) require high-memory server clusters that cannot run locally within hospital firewalls or on edge diagnostic workstations, severely hindering real-time clinical visual question answering.
motivation: Clinical workflows require rapid, interpretable diagnostic assistance on consumer hardware without sending private patient medical imagery over unvetted cloud APIs. Compressing visual tokens prior to language projection allows sub-2B models to preserve fine diagnostic features without running out of GPU memory.
method: Pairs a Convolutional Vision Transformer (CvT-24) image backbone with an architectural Token Packer module. The Token Packer downsamples high-resolution feature maps across spatial dimensions while preserving local clinical anomalies. Compressed visual embeddings are linearly projected into a fine-tuned 1.7B LLaMA language model.
architectureDiagram: Input Medical Scan [H×W×3] ➔ CvT-24 (Conv Projections) ➔ Token Packer (Spatial Compression: 256 ➔ 64 tokens) ➔ Linear Projection ➔ LLaMA 1.7B ➔ Clinical Diagnosis & Rationales

experimentalSetup.data: 120,000 curated biomedical image-caption and VQA pairs sourced from ROCO, MedQuAD, and clinical pathology archives.
experimentalSetup.compute: 1× NVIDIA RTX 4090 (24GB), PyTorch 2.2 with FlashAttention-2, mixed-precision FP16 training.
experimentalSetup.hyperparameters: AdamW optimizer, lr = 2e-5 with cosine decay, effective batch size = 32 (gradient accumulation = 4), weight decay = 0.05, 5 epochs.

results.summary: Achieved a 0.33 METEOR score on clinical question answering benchmarks under a sub-2B parameter budget. Baseline comparisons demonstrate competitive performance against significantly larger models while operating at a fraction of compute cost.

qualitativeExamples.title: Clinical Visual Question Answering Sample
qualitativeExamples.caption: Figure 1: MedOptm localized query response on an axial brain MRI scan. The prompt asks to differentiate between edema and mass boundary; the model highlights hyperintense T2 signals and correctly answers within 50 tokens.

qualitativeExamples.title: Token Compression Attention Map
qualitativeExamples.caption: Figure 2: Attention weight heatmaps before and after Token Packer reduction, verifying that high-gradient lesion borders retain high activation density after 75% token reduction.

limitations: Evaluated primarily on English-language biomedical captions; prone to hallucination on rare pediatric pathologies not represented in ROCO training splits; does not yet support multi-slice 3D volumetric context directly.
futureWork: Integrating 3D volumetric patch embeddings directly from NIfTI volumes, scaling training to 3D brain tumors, and conducting blinded physician utility evaluations.
reproduce:
git clone https://github.com/Devpatel1012/MedOptm
cd MedOptm
pip install -r requirements.txt
python eval_vqa.py --weights checkpoints/medoptm-1.9b.pt --benchmark roco_test

title: Brain MRI Surface Registration & Anatomical Alignment
subtitle: Deep learning framework for non-rigid 3D cortical surface mesh alignment from raw T1-weighted MRI scans.

reproducibility.weights: Preprocessed IXI Subject Distributed in Repo
reproducibility.data: IXI Dataset (Information eXtraction from Images, 560+ scans)
reproducibility.compute: Local workstations & FreeSurfer v7.4 recon-all pipeline

problem: 3D cortical surfaces feature complex, highly folded sulcal and gyral geometry that varies dramatically across subjects. Standard volumetric registration algorithms blur fine cortical boundaries and fail to guarantee surface topological consistency without self-intersections.
motivation: Neuroimaging studies require accurate point-to-point correspondence across subject cortical meshes to map functional and anatomical changes. Developing deep non-rigid registration directly on surface meshes circumvents volumetric blurring and dramatically accelerates multi-subject cohort studies.
method: Processes T1-weighted MRI through FreeSurfer's volumetric pipeline (recon-all) to extract white and pial cortical surfaces as .mgz and .obj meshes. Implements a surface deformation network operating on spherical parameterizations to minimize Chamfer surface distance while penalizing distortion energy and normal variance.
architectureDiagram: Raw T1 MRI ➔ FreeSurfer recon-all ➔ Spherical Conformal Mapping ➔ Deep Surface Deformation Network ➔ Topological Consistency Loss (Chamfer + Normal + Distortion) ➔ Aligned Cortical Mesh (.obj)

experimentalSetup.data: IXI benchmark dataset containing high-resolution T1 brain MRI scans from healthy adult subjects across 3 clinical hospital scanners.
experimentalSetup.compute: Linux workstation, FreeSurfer 7.4.1 (6-8 hours compute per subject for recon-all ground truth generation), PyTorch 3D for mesh rendering.
experimentalSetup.hyperparameters: Loss = Chamfer_Dist + 0.1 × Normal_Consistency + 0.05 × Mesh_Laplacian_Smoothness; lr = 1e-4, 100 epochs.

results.summary: Achieved significant reduction in mean surface distance while eliminating mesh face inversions across complex frontal and temporal sulci. Shipped a fully preprocessed IXI benchmark subject in the public repository to eliminate the multi-hour FreeSurfer barrier for other researchers.

qualitativeExamples.title: Cortical Mesh Alignment Overlay
qualitativeExamples.caption: Figure 1: Qualitative mesh alignment overlay inspected in Freeview. Green wireframe represents source subject pial mesh, purple surface represents fixed target brain, and gold mesh shows the registered output following non-rigid deformation.

qualitativeExamples.title: Sulcal Folding Geometry Detail
qualitativeExamples.caption: Figure 2: Close-up of the precentral gyrus showing curvature maps. The registration successfully preserves sulcal depth continuity without creating non-manifold vertices.

limitations: Currently requires initial volumetric skull-stripping and spherical parameterization via FreeSurfer; inference speed is rapid but upstream preprocessing remains computationally heavy; tested on healthy adult anatomy and needs validation on severe ventricular atrophy or tumor deformation.
futureWork: End-to-end direct voxel-to-mesh deformation predicting cortical surfaces in a single forward pass, bypassing the multi-hour FreeSurfer preprocessing requirement.
reproduce:

cd Brain-MRI-Surface-Registration
# Inspect preprocessed IXI subject surface in Freeview
freeview -v IXI002-Guys-0828-T1/mri/orig.mgz -f IXI002-Guys-0828-T1/surf/lh.pial:edgecolor=green

title: Fashion Multimodal Semantic Retrieval
subtitle: Cross-modal retrieval system mitigating relational attribute collapse in frozen text encoders via residual adapters and FAISS indexing.

reproducibility.compute: Google Colab Pro GPU (NVIDIA T4 / V100)

problem: Pre-trained vision-language contrastive models frequently suffer from relational attribute binding failure — treating 'blue jacket with black zipper' and 'black jacket with blue zipper' as near-identical vectors due to bag-of-words token aggregation in the text encoder.
motivation: Production e-commerce search requires fine-grained attribute fidelity at millisecond query latencies. Fine-tuning the entire dual-encoder is prohibitively expensive and risks catastrophic forgetting of general semantic concepts.
method: Trains a lightweight residual projection adapter on frozen FashionCLIP representations using hard negative contrastive pairs (where colors, textures, and garments are permuted). Embeddings are indexed using FAISS IVFFlat for sub-millisecond similarity search.
architectureDiagram: Text Query ➔ Frozen FashionCLIP Text Encoder ➔ Residual Projection Adapter ➔ Hard-Negative Relational Loss ➔ FAISS IVFFlat Index ➔ Top-K Disambiguated Candidates

experimentalSetup.data: Fashion200k benchmark supplemented with synthetic attribute-permuted negative text pairs.
experimentalSetup.compute: 1× NVIDIA T4 GPU (16GB), PyTorch, FAISS-GPU, Hugging Face Transformers.
experimentalSetup.hyperparameters: Residual adapter: 2-layer MLP with GELU, hidden dim 512, dropout 0.1, lr = 1e-4 with AdamW, batch size = 64, temperature = 0.07.

results.summary: Achieved significant improvements in Recall@K on attribute-swapped test suites while maintaining an average vector search latency under 0.8 milliseconds per query.

qualitativeExamples.title: Relational Disambiguation Before & After
qualitativeExamples.caption: Figure 1: Query comparison for 'striped blue shirt with white collar'. Frozen CLIP returns white shirts with blue stripes in top-3; our residual adapter retrieves exact striped garments with distinct white collars in ranks 1 through 5.

qualitativeExamples.title: t-SNE Embedding Separation
qualitativeExamples.caption: Figure 2: t-SNE projection of garment embeddings demonstrating clear geometric separation between permuted attribute clusters that overlap entirely in baseline CLIP space.

limitations: Hard-negative training pairs were synthetically generated and can introduce biases toward specific color adjectives; not yet evaluated on non-garment general retail categories; vocabulary bounded by FashionCLIP tokenizer.
futureWork: Extending relational adapter architectures to medical pathology reports to disambiguate left vs. right organ findings and lesion severity qualifiers.
reproduce:
git clone https://github.com/Devpatel1012/Fashion_Retrieval_Model
cd Fashion_Retrieval_Model
pip install -r requirements.txt
python search.py --query "blue shirt with black collar" --top_k 5

title: CvT-24: Convolutional Vision Transformer from First Principles
subtitle: Modular PyTorch implementation of the CvT-24 vision backbone with depthwise separable convolutional token projections.

reproducibility.weights: Custom PyTorch state_dict checkpoint available in repo

problem: Standard Vision Transformers (ViT) discard 2D shift-invariance and local spatial structure by flattening non-overlapping image patches into 1D sequences, requiring immense pre-training datasets to learn basic visual priors.
motivation: Implementing CvT-24 completely from scratch without external library wrappers provides granular control over positional embedding removal, convolutional token projections, and hierarchical downsampling stages. This architecture serves as the foundation for the MedOptm medical reasoning pipeline.
method: Replaces standard linear patch projections with depthwise separable convolutions in three hierarchical stages. The convolutional operations inject local inductive bias into the token embeddings while reducing sequence length, eliminating the need for explicit positional encodings.
architectureDiagram: Input [3×224×224] ➔ Stage 1: Conv Token Projection (stride 4) ➔ Transformer Blocks ➔ Stage 2: Conv Token Projection (stride 2) ➔ Transformer Blocks ➔ Stage 3: Conv Token Projection (stride 2) ➔ Global Average Pooling

experimentalSetup.data: Trained and benchmarked on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-100 validation splits.
experimentalSetup.compute: PyTorch 2.1, 1× NVIDIA RTX 3080 GPU, native FP16 AMP.
experimentalSetup.hyperparameters: AdamW, lr = 5e-4, weight decay = 0.05, warmup epochs = 10, cosine annealing scheduler over 100 epochs, RandAugment data augmentation.

results.summary: Verified mathematical equivalence and parameter count against official Microsoft CvT specifications while achieving faster convergence per parameter than vanilla ViT baselines.

qualitativeExamples.title: Hierarchical Feature Map Evolution
qualitativeExamples.caption: Figure 1: Visualization of intermediate convolutional token activations across Stage 1 (edge detection), Stage 2 (texture aggregation), and Stage 3 (semantic boundary formation).

qualitativeExamples.title: Multi-Head Self-Attention Patterns
qualitativeExamples.caption: Figure 2: Effective receptive field attention maps showing that convolutional projections produce localized attention heads in early layers and global coverage in late layers.

limitations: Depthwise convolutions introduce kernel memory access overhead that slightly reduces peak theoretical tensor-core throughput compared to pure matrix multiplication; custom modules require manual gradient checkpointing for large batch sizes.
futureWork: Authoring custom Triton kernels for fused depthwise-separable convolutional projection and self-attention to maximize memory bandwidth.
reproduce:
git clone https://github.com/Devpatel1012/cvt-24
cd cvt-24
python test_model.py --verify-params --stage-dims 64 192 384

title: BrainScan AI: Multi-Class MRI Diagnostic Interface
subtitle: Interactive clinical diagnostic system powered by two-stage transfer learning accepted at ICMLDE 2025.

reproducibility.weights: Pre-trained VGG16 model checkpoint in repository
reproducibility.data: Figshare & Kaggle multi-class brain MRI benchmark (3,264 scans)

problem: Brain tumor diagnosis on MRI requires differentiating subtle histological variations across glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumors. Heterogeneous scanner protocols and small sample sizes lead to rapid overfitting in deep neural networks.
motivation: A robust, lightweight two-stage transfer learning pipeline can adapt pre-trained feature hierarchies without disrupting low-level spatial filters, providing high clinical diagnostic reliability.
method: A two-stage training strategy using a modified VGG16 backbone: Stage 1 trains specialized dense classification heads and dropout regularizers while freezing convolutional feature extractors; Stage 2 unfreezes the top convolutional blocks with a lowered learning rate for fine-grained alignment.
architectureDiagram: Input MRI Scan ➔ Image Resizing & Intensity Normalization ➔ Frozen VGG16 Backbone ➔ Dense Head Training (Stage 1) ➔ Selective Block Unfreezing (Stage 2, lr=1e-5) ➔ 4-Class Softmax Output

experimentalSetup.data: 3,264 multi-sequence T1, T2, and FLAIR brain MRI scans spanning Glioma, Meningioma, Pituitary tumor, and Healthy control classes.
experimentalSetup.compute: NVIDIA T4 GPU, PyTorch, Scikit-learn, OpenCV, Streamlit.
experimentalSetup.hyperparameters: Stage 1: lr = 1e-3, 15 epochs; Stage 2: lr = 1e-5 with Adam optimizer, batch size = 32, categorical cross-entropy loss, data augmentation with rotation and zoom.

results.summary: Achieved 97.88% multi-class classification accuracy on hold-out test MRI scans. Presented and accepted at the International Conference on Machine Learning and Data Engineering (ICMLDE 2025).

qualitativeExamples.title: 4-Class Confusion Matrix
qualitativeExamples.caption: Figure 1: Normalized confusion matrix across Glioma (97.2%), Meningioma (96.8%), Pituitary (98.9%), and No Tumor (99.1%) classes on the hold-out test set of 653 scans.

qualitativeExamples.title: Inference Dashboard & Confidence Distribution
qualitativeExamples.caption: Figure 2: Real-time clinical diagnostic dashboard displaying MRI slice preview, class probability breakdown, and warning threshold alerts for borderline confidence scores.

limitations: Trained primarily on 2D axial MRI slices; performance may drop on coronal or sagittal planes without multi-view aggregation; scanner artifact robustness needs prospective multi-center clinical validation.
futureWork: Extending the two-stage protocol to full 3D volumetric segmentation models (such as 3D UNet or Swin UNETR) and generating Grad-CAM explainability heatmaps directly in the UI.
reproduce:

cd BrainTumorClassification-
pip install -r requirements.txt
streamlit run app.py
